denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Chronic kidney disease stage 1 was first diagnosed on 2025-03-13, AFTER the policy start date 2023-12-18; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial of Claim a48d04b4-793e-866e-e906-7f5281c2bd23 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period  

Claim Details:  
Claim ID: a48d04b4-793e-866e-e906-7f5281c2bd23  
Patient ID: a48d04b4-793e-866e-2186-bb359b053fd1  
Patient Name: Stanford Hoppe  
Policy: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (SGH‑GOLD)  
Coverage Start Date: 18‑12‑2023  
Date of Service / Diagnosis Onset: 13‑03‑2025  
Diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease stage 1  
Procedure: Patient referral for dental care  
Encounter Class: AMB  
Claim Amount: INR 14,124.72  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The diagnosis of Chronic kidney disease stage 1 was first recorded on 13‑03‑2025, which is after the policy start date of 18‑12‑2023. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_gold_policy#5]. Consequently, the 24‑month pre‑existing disease waiting period does not apply to this claim, as the waiting period is triggered only for conditions that meet the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease [suraksha_gold_policy#10].  

The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period is applicable. In this case, no documentary evidence has been provided to demonstrate that the kidney condition existed prior to the policy start date, as required by the denial standards [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].  

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating physician will attach clinical notes confirming that the referral for dental care is medically necessary for the management of the patient’s overall health, consistent with the policy’s definition of medically necessary treatment [suraksha_gold_policy#4].  

Reference to Denial Standards and Right to Appeal:  
We are exercising the right to appeal the denial within the 30‑day period stipulated in the claims procedure guidelines, and we are providing the required identification of the claim, denial reason, relevant policy clauses, and supporting clinical evidence as outlined in the grievance process [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8].  

Specific Request:  
In light of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be reprocessed, and the amount of INR 14,124.72 be paid in full to the provider.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (Clause 2.2) are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
citations.quote:
### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 2. Definitions > 2.1 Medically Necessary
citations.quote:
## 2. Definitions  
### 2.1 Medically Necessary
Treatment required for the medical management of the illness or injury, not exceeding the level of care necessary for safe, adequate and appropriate care, and prescribed by a medical practitioner in line with generally accepted standards of practice.
